newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK GIVES GO-AHEAD TO UNBUNDLING.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK GIVES GO-AHEAD TO UNBUNDLING.

text.p: Industrial holding company Malbak Ltd said on Monday it had decided to go ahead with a full unbundling of its underlying assets.
Malbak first announced in May it was was considering unbundling.

Implementation of the process will be influenced by the existence of pre-emptive rights in certain listed and unlisted investments and by the fact that it will not be practical to distribute unlisted securities to shareholders.
The company said it was intended that the unlisted investments would be realised for shareholders by listing or selling such investments.

"Any distribution of listed investments and the net proceeds from any realisation of unlisted investments are expected to be made during the first quarter of the 1997 calendar year," Malbak said in a statement.

Exchange controls would inhibit the distribution to most shareholders of shares in London-listed MY Holdings Plc , the company added. Various alternatives for dealing with this were being considered. Appropriate arrangements were also being considered for holders of Malbak ADRs and GDRs.

Sankorp Ltd, a major shareholder in the group, said it intended to either dispose of or reduce its holdings in the unbundled listed companies over time, with the possible exception of South African Druggists Ltd .
A final divided will be declared for Malbak's financial year ending August 31, but as a result of the restructuring, no interim dividend will be paid in the 1997 financial year.
Malbak said it expected to make another announcement on or about October 29, when it is due to publish preliminary results.
